subject: Clarify: session/retry pricing and partial-session charges
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brixton.io>

Cc: Finance AP <invoices@brixton.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on session pricing & partial responses

Hi Mina —

Thanks for taking a look. We're putting together an internal comparison of vendor economics for our real-time assistant and had a couple of questions specific to how you bill for streaming/continuous responses:

- Can you share the baseline hosted API rate card for 1:1 pricing (token rates for input/output) and the threshold/levels for volume discounts? We expect ~50M generated tokens/month in steady state.
- When a streaming response is interrupted (client disconnect, network blip, or local retry), how is billing handled for the partial generation that was in-flight? Do you prorate or bill per completed finished response?
- If the client retries the same request (e.g., resends with the same idempotency key), will we be double-billed for the repeated generation, or do you deduplicate at billing time?
- Any special considerations for function-calling flows where the model emits partial structured JSON then the client calls a function and resumes streaming?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call but wanted to get the baseline answers in writing first so procurement can model costs.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Product
Brixton Robotics
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on session pricing & partial responses

Hi Samir —

Appreciate the detail — helpful context. Quick answers up front, then a short technical note and next steps:

1) Baseline hosted API pricing (public, non-discounted):
   - Input tokens: $0.00080 per token
   - Output/generated tokens: $0.00120 per token
   - Embeddings / non-generation products are priced separately (I can send that sheet).

2) Volume discounts: at 50M generated tokens/month we typically discuss a committed discount tier — rough starter offer would be an 18% off list for a 12-month commitment at that volume. We can formalize in an SOW for Dedicated/Dedicated-like guarantees if you need SLAs.

3) Streaming / partial generations & disconnects (short version): billing is per generated token from our runtime. We do not require a successful client-side ACK to bill — tokens emitted by the model while the request was active are counted. That said, we have safeguards to prevent accidental double-billing for immediate automatic retries; see Priyom's note below.

4) Function-calling flows: tokens emitted before a function call are counted; resumed generations are billed for any additional tokens produced. We can discuss heuristics for conservative proration if you have complex chaining.

I've attached the Q1 rate card and a workspace cube with your projected numbers. Priyom is copied — he'll add a short technical note on idempotency and how retry/dedup works in practice.

If it helps, Karthik and I can do a 30-minute pricing + technical sync later this week to walk procurement through committed vs on-demand economics. Also can draft a usage-based quote for legal if you want to run numbers.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — that helps. A couple follow-ups so we can model worst-case spend:

- When you say "tokens emitted by the model while the request was active are counted", can you be explicit about the timing? Is a token considered billed when it is generated server-side, when it is sent to the client socket, or when the client successfully ACKs/reads it?
- If a client disconnects mid-response (e.g., user loses connectivity) and then immediately retries the same prompt with the same idempotency key, will Redwood deduplicate at the ledger level or will we be charged for both runs?
- What about retries where the client intentionally replays without idempotency (e.g., client-side bug) — do you have refund/proration policies in those cases?
- For function-calls: suppose the model outputs a partial JSON object, the client calls the function, and then a second streaming attempt resumes. Do you count the partial JSON tokens twice if the resumed generation re-emits overlapping tokens?

We want to avoid surprises in our forecasting. If you can put the rules in bullet form, procurement can map it to a cost model quickly.

—Samir
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@brixton.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on session pricing & partial responses

Hi all —

Short technical/billing clarification from the runtime side (putting it in plain bullets for procurement):

- Billing event: We record billing for tokens once the generator emits them into the server-side output stream (i.e., when the token is produced by the model runtime). We do not wait for the client TCP/HTTP ACK to charge.

- Streaming chunks vs tokens: We bill at token granularity. A streaming chunk is a transport unit; if a chunk contains N tokens, those N tokens are what get recorded.

- Disconnects: If the client disconnects mid-stream, any tokens already produced by the runtime before the disconnect are billed. Tokens that would have been produced after the disconnect are not billed.

- Retries & idempotency:
  - If the client retries the *same logical request* and supplies the same idempotency key (request-id) within the idempotency window (configurable but defaults to 10 minutes for us), we attempt server-side deduplication at the request level and will not double-bill for the identical generation ledger entry. This covers most accidental client retries and network glitches.
  - If the client resubmits without an idempotency key (or outside the window), it is treated as a new request and tokens produced will be billed separately.
  - If a retry resumes from a cursor (e.g., partial content persisted client-side and then resumed), we only bill for the delta tokens produced beyond the stored cursor if the resume uses the same logical session id. Best practice: include a resume cursor and idempotency key.

- Server-side automatic retries (transparent retries inside Redwood runtime to hide transient infra errors): these are not billed multiple times — the runtime collapses these into a single logical generation record before final commit.

- Function-calling / overlap: If the model emits a partial JSON then the client makes a function call and later asks the model to continue, we bill for tokens actually produced in each generation. If the resumed generation re-emits overlapping tokens (because the model re-generated the same prefix), those tokens are charged unless the client resumes with an explicit offset/resume cursor that prevents re-emission. We can provide a client SDK helper that enforces resume semantics to avoid overlap.

- Refunds/credits: For obvious platform errors (e.g., duplicate ledger entries due to our bug), we issue credits. For user-caused repeated submissions without idempotency, we do not issue credits. We can discuss an SLA or a manual review/case-by-case process if you need a softer stance for the trial period.

Hope this is clear — happy to provide a short spec doc that your infra team can implement for idempotency and resume.

—Priyom
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Samir —

Recap and next steps so procurement has a paper trail:

- Baseline list rates: input $0.00080 / token, output $0.00120 / token (see attached rate card).
- For 50M generated tokens/month we propose an 18% committed discount at 12-month term; we can show committed pricing vs on-demand in the quote.
- Streaming billing rules (short bullets you can paste into your model):
  * Billing recorded per generated token by the runtime as soon as it is produced.
  * Disconnects: tokens already produced are billed; tokens not produced are not billed.
  * Retries with idempotency key (within 10-minute window): deduped server-side, not double-billed.
  * Retries without idempotency / outside window: separate request → billed separately.
  * Server-side infra retries are collapsed by the runtime and not double-billed.
  * Function-calling: tokens are billed per actual tokens produced; overlap is billable unless you use resume offsets.

Action items:
- I will prepare a draft usage-based quote (list + committed tier) and send it by end of day Monday.
- Karthik will join a call if you want to run through legal/commit terms.
- Priyom will share a short idempotency/resume implementation guide for your engineering team (SDK snippet + recommended headers).

If Brixton wants, we can apply a one-off goodwill credit for the first month during pilot to reduce model risk while your infra integrates idempotency keys (we can discuss size on the call).

Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Monday 16 Feb at 10:00 PT to review the draft quote and the technical integration notes?

Best regards,
